definition: Enlarged heart; a heart that's bigger than what's typical. The heart may be unusually thick or dilated (stretched), short-term or permanent, and can affect the whole heart or just parts of it.
general_symptoms: Swelling, especially in your legs, feet or belly
general_causes: Any disease that makes your heart work harder
general_diagnosis_methods: Discussing symptoms, biological family health history, and physical activity
Physical exam (listening with stethoscope for heart murmur, checking for signs of heart failure like leg swelling, crackles in lungs, engorged neck veins)
general_treatments: Lifestyle changes (reduce salt intake, avoid tobacco use, eat heart-healthy foods, regular physical activity, stay at healthy weight, reduce alcohol intake, manage fluid intake)
Repairing or replacing a damaged heart valve
Placing a stent or performing coronary artery bypass surgery
general_outlook: Can be short-term or permanent depending on the cause
Can be serious or mild depending on the underlying condition
If caused by a short-term factor (like pregnancy or an infection), the heart returns to its usual size after treatment
If caused by a chronic condition, it usually won't go away and requires ongoing medication/treatment to manage symptoms
Early treatment can stop the condition from getting worse; earlier care gives better chances for a good outcome
complications: Blood clots (can lead to heart attack, stroke, or pulmonary embolism)
Heart failure (if left side is enlarged/left ventricular hypertrophy or dilated)
Sudden cardiac death (from deadly abnormal heart rhythms)
prevention: Being physically active for 150 minutes per week (30 minutes 5 times per week)
Managing blood pressure, blood sugar, and cholesterol
Maintaining a weight that's healthy for you
Avoiding use of tobacco products and other addictive substances

underlying_causes_and_conditions.mechanism: Can cause inflammation in your heart muscle
Conditions that deposit substances in your heart

underlying_causes_and_conditions.cause_name: Diseases that make your heart pump a lot of blood

examples: hole in the wall between the left and right sides

underlying_causes_and_conditions.mechanism: Damage in your heart from unmanaged, long-term high blood pressure
Causes fluid buildup, forcing heart to pump more fluid
Narrow or leaky valves keeping blood from flowing normally

underlying_causes_and_conditions.notes: Heart function is normal (or better) despite enlargement

risk_factors: History of the condition in biological family
Heavy alcohol use or substance use disorder
Personal or family history of heart attacks
